transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Aurora, Head of ML), Tom Nguyen (Aurora, Platform Eng), Sara Bennett (Aurora, VP Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Discussed POC timeline and milestones: kickoff, access setup, initial benchmarks, mid-point review, exec readout. Agreed on success criteria around latency, throughput, and quality (ROC AUC / accuracy on de-identifed data). ACTIONS: Redwood to send pricing + SOC2/HIPAA docs; Aurora to provide sample dataset and request traces; schedule kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jared from redwood, i'll kick us off. um basic agenda is to scope the poc timeline and milestones and make sure we all agree on success criteria. priya from our se team will go into sizing and bench approach.
[00:22] Marta: hi, thanks, excited. short background — aurora is evaluating an on-prem or vpc option because most of our data is phm, so HIPAA is a requirement. we want a 6-weekish poc to validate latency, cost, and safety controls.
[00:40] Priya: great, yeah i'll try to be pragmatic. first question, what's the primary workload? is this chat triage, clinical summarization, or embeddings for search?
[00:52] Tom: primarily clinical summarization and triage with about 400 concurrent users at peak. average request size is about 800 tokens in and 200-400 out. we also want embeddings for search on historical notes but that's a secondary workload.
[01:10] Priya: ok 800 tokens input that's helpful. rough sizing note — for hosted vs dedicated: hosted api will get you up quickly, but if you need predictable tail latency and HIPAA/air-gapped controls, dedicated or private is better. For POC we can do dedicated reserved pool or a private deployment in your VPC.
[01:36] Sara: to be clear, security is non-negotiable. we need SOC2 + HIPAA and audit logs, and keys managed by our KMS. also SSO/SAML for console access.
[01:48] Priya: yes we support KMS integrations and audit logs — i'll send the compliance pack after. note: sometimes our compliance doc references "Redwood Dedicate" which is our dedicated tier, apologies for the transcript mis-say.
[02:01] Marta: that helps. success criteria from our side: 1) < 400ms p95 for triage-ish calls, 2) output quality at least parity with our baseline model (we'll provide evaluation prompts and labels), and 3) deployment that doesn't leak PHI and passes our security review.
[02:22] Jared: good concise criteria. i'll put those into the poc acceptance section. timeline thoughts: kickoff next week, 2 weeks for access+setup, 1 week initial benchmark, 1 week tuning, then midpoint review around week 3 or 4, and exec readout at week 6. does that match your expectation?
[02:45] Tom: yes that aligns but we might have some internal procurement lead-time for network peering. estimated 5 business days to get infra approvals.
[02:58] Priya: ok factor that in. proposed milestones: kickoff (2026-07-13), access setup & network (target 2026-07-20), initial benchmark run (2026-07-24), mid-point review with tuning recommendations (2026-08-03), exec readout (2026-08-17).
[03:18] Sara: those dates look reasonable. can you define the benchmark we will run? what metrics and what dataset?
[03:26] Priya: yes — benchmark plan: run 10k representative requests (mix of 70% summarization, 30% triage) across a few model variants. capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, cost per 1k responses, and quality metrics — we'll compute BLEU or ROUGE where applicable and a custom accuracy metric against labeled set.
[03:48] Marta: on quality we'll share a labeled set of ~500 de-identified cases and a scoring rubric. we expect redwood to run the eval and provide the raw outputs.
[03:59] Priya: perfect. also we'll log hallucination rates and do a brief safety check — we can surface the outputs in a secure s3 share.
[04:10] Jared: logistic note — i'll send the pricing template and a POC scope doc. will include acceptance criteria and a short list of models we recommend to test (open models and a couple of quantized variants).
[04:22] Tom: network question — for vpc/private mode do you require dedicated hosts or can you route via peering? we prefer peering to avoid moving data.
[04:33] Priya: we support both. for strict compliance we often do a private deployment with customer-managed networking; peering is fine for many customers. we'll provide a network checklist.
[04:43] Speaker 1: [inaudible] can you also detail the KMS flow?
[04:47] Priya: yes — keys stay in your KMS and we integrate via key wrap. i'll include an architecture diagram in the compliance pack.
[04:55] Marta: what's the expected cost delta between quantized and non-quantized profiles? rough ballpark.
[05:02] Priya: typically 2-4x savings on GPU hours with 4-bit quantization depending on model and perf tradeoffs; we'll present concrete numbers in the pricing sheet and run the bench both with and without quantization.
[05:18] Jared: for success criteria we'll also add a cost-per-1k-responses target so the execs can evaluate economics. sara, does that work?
[05:25] Sara: yes, we'll need a simple $/1k metric plus a projected monthly run-rate for production.
[05:31] Priya: note on throughput: continuous batching can help reduce cost but might increase tail latency; we'll surface a latency vs cost curve in the mid-point report so you can choose tradeoffs.
[05:45] Tom: for the initial benchmark, what infra will you spin up? GPUs, instance types?
[05:51] Priya: for the POC we'll likely recommend an A100-equivalent type for high throughput runs, and maybe an H100 or L4 variant if lower latency is critical — we'll include suggested instance types in the sizing doc.
[06:03] Marta: timeline detail — when do you need our sample data and request traces?
[06:07] Jared: asap, ideally by next friday 2026-07-10. Tom: is that feasible?
[06:13] Tom: yes we can share redacted data extracts and a set of 1k sample requests by then, i'll coordinate with security.
[06:19] Priya: perfect. also can you share request distribution — concurrent users, typical inter-request spacing — that helps our batching sim.
[06:29] Tom: will include that.
[06:32] Marta: regarding evaluation we'll want both automated metrics and a small manual review by clinicians at mid-point. okay?
[06:38] Priya: yes we'll schedule a short clinician readout during the mid-point review.
[06:43] Jared: quick question about fallback policies: if latency spikes do you want to failover to a smaller cheaper model or queue requests?
[06:52] Sara: prefer failover to a smaller model that preserves quality as much as possible. avoid long queues.
[06:58] Priya: we can configure smart routing to fallback to compatible variants; that's standard in our runtime.
[07:04] Marta: are there any blockers from your side around regulatory sign-off?
[07:08] Sara: procurement will likely need our legal to review the DPA, and we may need a quick security questionnaire answer.
[07:16] Jared: we'll surface our standard DPA and a security questionnaire. Priya will attach SOC2 & HIPAA docs.
[07:23] Priya: i'll also include our recommended data handling and de-id checklist so you can confirm no PHI is shared during bench.
[07:31] Jared: ok next up — milestones recap: kickoff 7/13, access & network by 7/20, bench run by 7/24, tuning 7/27, mid-point 8/3, exec 8/17. any concerns?
[07:45] Tom: procurement could push access out; i'll prioritize getting approvals.
[07:50] Marta: i'm comfortable with the plan as long as we stick to mid-point clinician review.
[07:55] Sara: same. please include crisp acceptance criteria in the POC doc — e.g. p95 latency <400ms, quality >= baseline on labeled set, $/1k under X (we'll refine).
[08:08] Jared: will do. I'll also attach a benchmark spreadsheet link for visibility: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/aurora-poc (note: placeholder link).
[08:18] Priya: one more technical note — for embeddings we'll test CPU vs GPU inference cost tradeoffs and recommend caching strategies for repeated queries.
[08:28] Tom: yes caching would be helpful. do you have tooling to manage prefix cache or kv cache?
[08:33] Priya: our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; we'll show cache hit rate impact in the mid-point report.
[08:41] Marta: any legal caveats for showing raw outputs in shared s3? we need to ensure retention policies.
[08:47] Priya: retention can be configured and we'll follow your policy; we'll document the retention & purge steps.
[08:54] Sara: okay. from exec readout perspective, we want a 15-minute summary with cost/latency/quality and recommendation (go/no-go).
[09:02] Jared: agreed. We'll prepare a 15-min exec deck with those slides at the end.
[09:07] Marta: final ask: can you run a small spike on-prem for latency comparison?
[09:11] Priya: yes we can set up a micro-benchmark if you give us access to a test host in your network. that's part of the access checklist.
[09:20] Tom: i'll try to have a host ready by 7/20.
[09:24] Jared: awesome. any other competitors or alternatives you are actively evaluating?
[09:29] Sara: we're also seeing demos from Anthropic and OpenAI hosted options; Vertex AI is being considered for embeddings. cost and compliance are the tie-breakers.
[09:40] Priya: noted. we'll try to show comparative numbers where possible.
[09:45] Jared: ok wrap-up: i will send POC doc + pricing, priya sends compliance pack + sizing, tom will share data and infra details, and we'll schedule kickoff for 7/13.
[09:57] Marta: thanks everyone.
[10:00] Meeting ends.

References and shared artifacts mentioned:
- POC scope & pricing (Jared) - link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/poc/aurora-scope

- Compliance & architecture pack (Priya) - will include SOC 2, HIPAA notes, network diagram
notes: POC duration: ~6 weeks (kickoff to exec readout)
Primary success criteria: p95 latency <400ms, quality >= baseline on labeled set, acceptable $/1k responses
Milestones: kickoff, access setup, initial benchmark, tuning, mid-point review, exec readout
